# Purpose and data protection

This notebook documents a reproducible workflow for analyzing single-cell RNA-seq count matrices produced by a pipeline compatible with the 10x format. It is an anonymized copy of the analysis: it contains no data, results, personal paths, original sample names, experimental conditions, or restricted references.

The data/ directory is excluded from Git. Before executing this notebook, create config/samples.csv locally from config/example_samples.csv and confirm it will not be versioned.

# 1. Setup

## Packages

~~~{r libraries}
library(Seurat)
library(tidyverse)
library(patchwork)

# Required only when nuclear fraction will be calculated from BAM files:
# library(DropletQC)
# library(Rsamtools)
~~~

## Local configuration

Relative paths prevent disclosure of workstation structure. The configuration table should have one row per library and the columns sample_id, group, count_matrix_dir, and, if applicable, bam_path.

~~~{r config}
stopifnot(file.exists("config/samples.csv"))
samples <- readr::read_csv("config/samples.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
stopifnot(all(c("sample_id", "group", "count_matrix_dir") %in% names(samples)))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(samples$sample_id))

# Retain only metadata needed for analytical traceability.
samples <- samples |> dplyr::select(sample_id, group, count_matrix_dir, bam_path)
~~~

# 2. Count-matrix import and initial quality control

## Load count matrices

Each matrix must correspond to a previously processed library and contain unnormalized counts. If Read10X() returns a multimodal list, explicitly select the gene-expression modality.

~~~{r load-counts}
count_matrices <- purrr::set_names(samples$count_matrix_dir, samples$sample_id) |>
  purrr::map(Read10X)

count_matrices <- purrr::map(count_matrices, \(x) {
  if (is.list(x)) x[["Gene Expression"]] else x
})
~~~

## Create Seurat objects and calculate QC metrics

Calculate mitochondrial percentage and a complexity metric (log10GenesPerUMI). Adapt the mitochondrial gene pattern to the naming convention of the reference in use.

~~~{r create-seurat}
seurat_objects <- purrr::imap(count_matrices, \(counts, sample_name) {
  obj <- CreateSeuratObject(
    counts = counts,
    project = sample_name,
    min.cells = 3,
    min.features = 200
  )
  obj[["percent.mt"]] <- PercentageFeatureSet(obj, pattern = "^mt-")
  obj$log10GenesPerUMI <- log10(obj$nFeature_RNA) / log10(obj$nCount_RNA)
  obj$sample_id <- sample_name
  obj$group <- samples$group[match(sample_name, samples$sample_id)]
  obj
})

qc_metadata <- purrr::map(seurat_objects, \(x) x[[]]) |> dplyr::bind_rows()
~~~

## Inspect QC distributions

Do not inherit thresholds from another cohort. Review every sample, the metric distributions, and their joint patterns before deciding exclusions.

~~~{r qc-plots}
all_cells <- merge(seurat_objects[[1]], y = seurat_objects[-1])
VlnPlot(
  all_cells,
  features = c("nFeature_RNA", "nCount_RNA", "percent.mt"),
  group.by = "sample_id", ncol = 3, pt.size = 0
)

qc_metadata |>
  ggplot(aes(nCount_RNA, percent.mt, colour = sample_id)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.25, size = 0.2) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  theme_classic()
~~~

# 4. Normalization, dimensionality reduction, and initial clustering

Normalize each sample separately first to identify technical anomalies. Then merge libraries and reprocess the combined object. Choose the number of principal components and the clustering resolution using diagnostics rather than copying values from another run.

~~~{r normalize-per-sample}
seurat_processed <- purrr::map(seurat_objects, \(obj) {
  obj |>
    NormalizeData(verbose = FALSE) |>
    FindVariableFeatures(verbose = FALSE) |>
    ScaleData(verbose = FALSE) |>
    RunPCA(verbose = FALSE)
})

ElbowPlot(seurat_processed[[1]])
~~~

~~~{r merge-and-cluster}
combined <- merge(
  x = seurat_objects[[1]],
  y = seurat_objects[-1],
  add.cell.ids = names(seurat_objects)
)

combined <- combined |>
  NormalizeData(verbose = FALSE) |>
  FindVariableFeatures(verbose = FALSE) |>
  ScaleData(verbose = FALSE) |>
  RunPCA(verbose = FALSE) |>
  FindNeighbors(dims = 1:30, verbose = FALSE) |>
  FindClusters(resolution = c(0.2, 0.5, 1.0), verbose = FALSE) |>
  RunUMAP(dims = 1:30, verbose = FALSE)
~~~

## Cluster diagnostics

~~~{r cluster-diagnostics}
DimPlot(combined, group.by = "sample_id") + DimPlot(combined, group.by = "group")
FeaturePlot(combined, features = c("nCount_RNA", "nFeature_RNA", "percent.mt"))
VlnPlot(combined, features = c("nCount_RNA", "nFeature_RNA", "percent.mt"), pt.size = 0)
~~~

# 5. Markers and population identification

Annotation should be supported by literature markers or references that the analyst is authorized to use. Keep a marker list in local configuration if it reveals non-shareable study details.

~~~{r markers}
Idents(combined) <- "RNA_snn_res.0.5"  # choose after diagnostic review
cluster_markers <- FindAllMarkers(
  combined,
  only.pos = TRUE,
  min.pct = 0.25,
  logfc.threshold = 0.25
)

# Example: load an approved local marker table that is not versioned.
# marker_panel <- readr::read_csv("private/marker_panel.csv")
# DotPlot(combined, features = marker_panel$gene) + RotatedAxis()
~~~

# 6. Iterative filtering and reprocessing

Document filtering decisions and apply them as an explicit cluster vector or a justified QC rule. Do not encode original cluster numbers, thresholds, or cell-population names here.

~~~{r filter-round-1}
# Complete this only after reviewing QC, markers, and sample composition.
clusters_to_remove <- character(0)

filtered <- subset(
  combined,
  idents = setdiff(levels(Idents(combined)), clusters_to_remove)
)

filtered <- filtered |>
  NormalizeData(verbose = FALSE) |>
  FindVariableFeatures(verbose = FALSE) |>
  ScaleData(verbose = FALSE) |>
  RunPCA(verbose = FALSE) |>
  FindNeighbors(dims = 1:30, verbose = FALSE) |>
  FindClusters(resolution = c(0.2, 0.5, 1.0), verbose = FALSE) |>
  RunUMAP(dims = 1:30, verbose = FALSE)
~~~

Repeat QC plots, the cell distribution by sample, and marker review after each filtering round. If nuclear fraction is calculated, retain the previously added values and check that they do not introduce library- or cluster-specific bias.

~~~{r filtered-qc}
DimPlot(filtered, group.by = "sample_id")
FeaturePlot(filtered, features = c("nCount_RNA", "nFeature_RNA", "percent.mt"))
table(filtered$sample_id, Idents(filtered))
~~~

## Pre-publication checklist

- [ ] No count matrices, BAM/FASTQ files, R objects, metadata, or results are versioned.
- [ ] Paths are relative and disclose no accounts, machines, or locations.
- [ ] Original identifiers were replaced with generic values.
- [ ] Git status shows no ignored files staged for commit.
- [ ] R and package versions are captured in a local report or a reviewed lockfile.
